prompt: A single cutaway illustration of a small, transparent, nine-square-metre autonomous retail capsule on a street corner, showing a shopper entering without staff while overhead sensors and cameras track a packaged snack, a toy, and a medicine being lifted from shelves and automatically charged to a phone; on one side, a compact vending panel and robotic kiosk dispense items, while a robot arm restocks a shelf and attempts to hand over a product; nearby, small visual vignettes show the system’s limits—a spilled drink, a confused customer, an oddly shaped item the gripper cannot grasp, and a wheelchair user checking accessibility—while in the background a faint, oversized supermarket silhouette suggests a harder, larger version of the same idea, and a glowing 24-hour sign conveys continuous operation, presenting autonomous retail not as a finished store but as an experimental machine for everyday commerce.
